_comment: Documented usage-window (quota) endpoints, keyed by models.dev provider id.
Data, not code: an operator can add a provider here without touching Python.
Consumed by `scripts/quota_probe.py`, which probes these endpoints and writes the
verdict into a cache that downstream tooling reads when reporting rate-limit and
usage information. This is separate from account balance (credit-endpoints.json),
which answers 'is this account funded'; this file answers 'how much usage window
is left before hitting a limit'.
Only providers with a DOCUMENTED, first-party usage-window endpoint belong here.
Most providers publish none. Absence of a provider's id in this file means the
provider does not report usage windows — the value is never estimated or inferred.
Entry fields:
url      absolute https endpoint (GET)
auth     bearer | x-api-key | raw (header named by auth_header)
doc      citation for the response shape below
windows  REQUIRED, array of one or more window entries, each with:
window  one of: session | daily | weekly | subscription
signals ORDERED list, most precise first; the first one PRESENT in the
response decides. Each signal has:
path  list of dict keys / integer list indices
[] (empty) means the root object itself
type  amount_used          number of units consumed
amount_remaining    units left before hitting limit
limit_total         total capacity of this window
percent_remaining   % of limit remaining
reset_at            ISO 8601 timestamp when window resets
reset_in_seconds    seconds until window resets
unit_literal        fixed known unit string (used with value field)
account_blocked     true => account cannot make requests
account_blocked_negated false => account can make requests
minus optional path subtracted from a balance/limit (spent-to-date)
value only for unit_literal; a fixed string naming the unit
desc  what the field actually means, for the audit trail
account_signals optional, for account-level status not tied to a specific window
Ordering matters: a field that is exact but often null must come before a
coarser field that is always present, or the coarse one would mask it.

signals.desc: credits left under this key's spending cap; null when the key is uncapped
the key's total spending cap; null when uncapped
credits consumed so far under this key

cadence label for when the cap resets (e.g. "daily", "monthly"), null if it never resets -- NOT a timestamp, informational only (T038-independent-review finding I2); resolve_window does not yet consume this type
